result.summary:
WF-02 STEP 2c SECURITY GATE — REQ-193 — VERDICT: FAIL.

Diff reviewed: git diff main...HEAD -- lib/ config/ (scoped to REQ-193 artifacts: lib/letflow/obs/logger.ex [new], config/config.exs, config/runtime.exs). The lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex changes in the same diff are tagged REQ-198 and were security-reviewed separately (PASS); they are not re-reviewed here.

=== SCOPE TEST ===

In scope for security review:
- lib/letflow/obs/logger.ex (new): a :logger_formatter that resolves and processes log metadata including potential secret values — directly relevant to INV-4.
- config/config.exs: configures OTP :default_handler formatter to Letflow.Obs.Logger.
- config/runtime.exs: reads LOG_LEVEL env var, configures :logger level at boot.

Not triggered:
- No priv/repo/migrations changes.
- No API routes reading/writing tenant-scoped data.
- No lookup-by-ID handlers.
- No tenant-scoped Ecto schema modules.
- LOG_LEVEL is an operational config value, not a secret — the runtime.exs change does not resolve a secret.

=== INV-1 (Tenant data isolation) ===
NOT-APPLICABLE. No DB queries, no Ecto schema modules, no migrations, no tenant-scoped data access in this diff.

=== INV-2 (Server-side field authorization) ===
NOT-APPLICABLE. No API routes or response-shaping code (S4 not started).

=== INV-3 (Untrusted runtime sandboxing) ===
NOT-APPLICABLE. S5 not started.

=== INV-4 (Secrets by reference only) — APPLIES — FAIL ===

The logger is the primary enforcement boundary for secret non-leakage in log output. Two paths through encode_entry/3 were examined:

NORMAL PATH — PASS:
  stripped = Map.drop(meta, @beam_reserved_keys)
  {clean, violations} = split_reserved(stripped)
  additional = clean |> redact_sensitive() |> Map.new(...)
  Jason.encode!(Map.merge(additional, base))
redact_sensitive/1 is called on `clean` (meta with BEAM reserved keys and formatter-reserved keys stripped) BEFORE Jason.encode!. The normal encoding path is correct.

RESCUE/FALLBACK PATH — BLOCKER:
  rescue
    e ->
      fallback = %{
        ...
        "message" => "log encoding failed: #{inspect({level, msg, meta, e})}"
      }
      Jason.encode!(fallback)
Here `meta` is the ORIGINAL, UNREDACTED metadata map passed to encode_entry/3 — it is NOT the post-redact_sensitive/1 `additional` variable. The rescue block is reached when Jason.encode!/1 raises on the primary path, which happens when metadata contains a struct that does not implement Jason.Encoder. safe_value/1 converts pid/reference/function/port to inspect strings but has a catch-all `defp safe_value(v), do: v` that passes structs through unchanged — any struct in metadata will cause Jason.encode! to raise, triggering this path.

If that same metadata map also contains a sensitive key (e.g., :password, :token, :authorization, :client_secret), its plaintext value is emitted via inspect(meta) in the fallback message, completely bypassing redact_sensitive/1. This is an INV-4 violation: secrets must never appear in log output.

Required fix: replace `meta` in the inspect call with a safe version that cannot contain sensitive values. Minimal fix — use a redacted version:
  "log encoding failed: #{inspect({level, msg, redact_sensitive(Map.drop(meta, @beam_reserved_keys)), e})}"
Alternatively, omit meta from the fallback message entirely:
  "log encoding failed (metadata omitted): level=#{inspect(level)}"

Route back to ELIXIR-DEV with this specific fix required before re-gate.

Hardcoded-secret check (INV-4 How to verify): Select-String across lib/letflow/obs/logger.ex, config/config.exs, config/runtime.exs for pattern matching secret literals — no hits. No hardcoded secrets found.

=== INV-5 (Not-found/forbidden indistinguishability) ===
NOT-APPLICABLE. No multi-tenant lookup-by-ID endpoints (S4 not started).

=== INV-6 (New data-access paths prove their scoping) ===
NOT-APPLICABLE. No new data-access paths.

=== INV-7 (No SQL string interpolation) ===
NOT-APPLICABLE. No SQL in this diff.

=== INV-8 (No unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths) — APPLIES — PASS ===

The Jason.encode!/1 call on the primary path is wrapped in try/rescue — encoding failures are handled. The fallback Jason.encode!/1 operates on a plain string-to-string map and cannot raise in practice. No bare {:ok, _} = matches on external I/O found in logger.ex (verified via grep). safe_value/1 prevents crash-loop conditions for BEAM-native non-JSON types.

OBSERVATION (no additional severity): safe_value/1's catch-all `defp safe_value(v), do: v` passes arbitrary structs through to Jason, which raises. The rescue catches this — no crash loop. The degradation is graceful. The concern is the unredacted meta in the fallback message, which is the INV-4 BLOCKER above.

=== ADDITIONAL LOGGER-SPECIFIC CHECKS ===

(a) redact_sensitive/1 before Jason.encode!/1: PASS on normal path; BLOCKER on rescue path (see INV-4 above).

(b) Re-entry guard for reserved-field violation warnings: PASS. format/2 checks Map.get(meta, :formatter_violation) == true before calling encode_entry/3. The :logger.warning/3 call that fires on reserved-field violations passes %{formatter_violation: true} in its metadata map, so if it routes back through this formatter, format/2 takes the plain-text branch and returns without calling encode_entry/3 again. No infinite recursion.

(c) Non-serializable metadata crash-loop: PASS. safe_value/1 handles pid/ref/fun/port. Structs without Jason.Encoder fall through the catch-all, cause Jason.encode! to raise, which is caught by the rescue block — no crash loop. The formatter does not crash the OTP logger handler on non-serializable input.

(d) LOG_LEVEL invalid value exposure in error message (runtime.exs): MINOR. `raise "Invalid LOG_LEVEL=#{inspect(invalid)}"` exposes the invalid env var value in the startup error message. LOG_LEVEL is operator-controlled input (not tenant/user input), and this fires at boot time before any request handling, so this is not a user-data exposure. Noted for completeness; not a BLOCKER.

=== VERDICT ===
FAIL. One BLOCKER (INV-4): rescue path in encode_entry/3 (lib/letflow/obs/logger.ex line ~123) includes inspect(meta) where meta is unredacted, allowing sensitive metadata values to bypass redact_sensitive/1 and appear in the fallback log message. Route back to ELIXIR-DEV with the required fix before re-gate.

If Jason.encode! raises (triggered by any struct without Jason.Encoder in metadata — safe_value/1 only covers pid/ref/fun/port), any sensitive key in meta (:password, :token, :authorization, :client_secret, etc.) is emitted in plaintext in the fallback message. This bypasses redact_sensitive/1 entirely and violates INV-4.
issues.fix_required: Replace `meta` in the rescue inspect call with a redacted version: `redact_sensitive(Map.drop(meta, @beam_reserved_keys))`, or omit meta from the fallback message entirely.
